 Order
Heard Sri Srinivas B. Naik, learned counsel for the petitioner and Smt.Kirtilata R.Patil, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.

2. The petitioner is before this Court seeking regular bail in Crime No.62/2024 of Gadag Rural Police Station (on the file of 2ND Additional Civil Judge and JMFC-II, Gadag) registered for the offences punishable U/S 498A, 304B R/W 149 OF IPC, and under Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
3. It is the case of the prosecution that the brother of the deceased lodged a complaint stating that on 13.04.2022, they performed the marriage of his sister with accused No.1.
After the marriage, his sister was very happily residing in her matrimonial home for one year.
Thereafter, the family members along with accused No.1 were on one or the other way demanding the dowry from his sister.
4. It is further stated in the complaint that, his sister had not begotten a child even after two years of her marriage.
That was also one of the prime factors for demanding dowry NC: 2024:KHC-D:7900 and harassing his sister.
On 27.03.2024, around 10.36am, he had received a message from his sister to bring her documents relating to her school and college which were in his house.
On 11.20am, he received a message stating that his sister had committed suicide.
Immediately, he went to the house and saw that his sister was dead.
Therefore, he lodged a complaint.
5. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the complainant made false and baseless allegations without assigning the overt act properly against each accused.
The allegations made against the petitioners are omnibus, baseless.
The petitioners had not harassed, ill-treated the deceased in her matrimonial home.
6. It is further submitted that the petitioners in fact were taking care of her nicely and even they did not know the reason behind the said suicide.
Mere making allegations against the petitioners without any basis is not sufficient to deny the bail.
The petitioners are permanent residents of Adavisomapur and they were the earning members of their family.
They will abide the conditions imposed by this Court, in the event of their release on bail.
Making such submission, the learned counsel for the petitioners prays to allow the petition.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader vehemently opposed the bail petition and submitted that the petitioners have committed heinous offence.
They committed murder of the young and innocent woman who had dream in her mind to build her life in her matrimonial home.
8. It is further submitted that the brother of the deceased who is the complainant herein had stated in his complaint the harassment, ill-treatment and demand of dowry by the petitioners.
The petitioner No.1 being a husband and petitioner No.4 being a brother-in-law had to take care of the young woman whom she went to their house with a hope of bright future.
Since they have committed heinous offence, they are not entitled for any relief.
Making such submission, the learned HCGP prays to dismiss the petition.

9. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the averments of the charge sheet, it appears that the marriage between the first petitioner and the deceased had taken place on 13.04.2022.
According to the complainant, his sister was very happy for one year in her matrimonial home.
Thereafter, she was being harassed, ill- NC: 2024:KHC-D:7900 treated in connection with demand of dowry and also for not having a child even after two years of her marriage.

10. On reading of the entire complaint, though the complainant made allegations regarding harassment and ill- treatment in connection with demand of dowry, no specific overt act is attributed against the petitioners.
Mere making omnibus allegations regarding the said ill-treatment and harassment is not sufficient to deny the bail.

Therefore, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioners are ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.62/2024 of respondent Police Station, on executing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
each (Rupees One lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Trial Court, subject to the following conditions:
a) The petitioners shall not threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses nor hamper the proceedings of the Court.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:7900 b) The petitioners shall appear before the Trial Court on all dates of hearing without fail.
In case, if the petitioners violate any of the bail conditions as stated above, the prosecution will be at liberty to seek for cancellation of bail.
